ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a negative feedback control block diagram. The input R(s) enters the summing point; the upper/left side of the summing point is the positive-sign input, and the feedback end is the negative-sign input; the forward channel successively passes through the gain block K_a and the motor transfer function block 10/(1+10s), and the output is ω(s); the output signal returns to the negative end of the summing point through a feedback line with no additional gain label, so it is unit negative feedback. Reasoning: The open-loop motor transfer function is 10/(1+10s), and its time constant τ_ol = 10. From the forward channel in the figure, after adding the amplifier, the forward transfer function is G(s)=K_a·10/(1+10s). The unit negative feedback closed-loop transfer function is T(s)=G(s)/(1+G(s)) = [10K_a/(1+10s)] / [1+10K_a/(1+10s)] = 10K_a/(1+10s+10K_a). Write the denominator as (1+10K_a)[1 + (10/(1+10K_a))s], so the closed-loop time constant τ_cl = 10/(1+10K_a). The problem requires that the closed-loop time constant be reduced by 100 times compared with the open-loop time constant, namely τ_cl = 10/100 = 0.1. Solve the equation 10/(1+10K_a)=0.1, obtaining 1+10K_a=100, therefore K_a=9.9, approximately 10.
